articles.title: El RCT Barcelona de Marc López gana el Nacional por equipos ante el Chamartín
articles.standfirst: Es el título número 36 del club catalán
articles.summary: Es el título número 36 del club catalán
articles.body: El RCT Barcelona-1899 se ha proclamado una vez más campeón de España por equipos masculinos -el pasado miércoles ganó también la competición femenina- tras superar 1-4 a los anfitriones del Club de Tenis Chamartín en la final del LVI Campeonato de España de la categoría. Es el primer doblete que logra desde 2019. Así, el RCT Barcelona-1899 se resarce de la final perdida el pasado año ante el Real Murcia CT 1919 y levanta su título número 36 en las 56 ediciones disputadas. También mantiene su imbatibilidad en finales frente al Club de Tenis Chamartín, a quien ha ganado las ocho que han disputado. Los madrileños buscaban el colofón a la celebración de su 60º Aniversario con un título que ganaron por última vez hace 13 años. El primero, en 1985, lo convirtió en el primer club no barcelonés en coronarse campeón de España. Como es tradicional en este torneo los participantes alinearon escuadras de gran nivel, aunque los tenistas de primera fila de nuestro tenis ya no disputan una competición a la que antes eran asiduos por coincidir sus fechas ahora con el circuito ATP. Con todo, la final arrancó con el triunfo barcelonés de Àlex Martí Pujolràs sobre Sergi Pérez Contri por 6-3 6-1, pero los locales igualaron gracias a la remontada de Alejandro Moro frente a Roberto Carballés (1-6 6-3 6-2). El conjunto catalán se adelantó de nuevo con trabajados triunfos de Oriol Roca ante Alejo Sánchez Quílez por 6-4 4-6 7-5 y de Daniel Rincón frente a Miguel Damas por 3-6 6-3 6-1. Y el punto decisivo, no menos disputado, lo ganó Max Alcalá frente al lituano Vilius Gaubas 6-3 3-6 6-4. Cuatro de los cinco partidos, como vemos, se decidieron en cinco sets. Los capitanes son también muestra del alto nivel de la competición. Al frente del R.C.T. Barcelona estaba Marc López, futuro capitán de Copa Davis que reconoció su "orgullo máximo, no solo por mí, sino por todos los compañeros. Al final el marcador marca el 4-1, pero ha sido muy duro, ha habido muchos partidos muy duros y, por suerte, ha caído de nuestro lado.” El capitán del Chamartín, Guillermo García López mostró orgulloso de su equipo a pesar de la derrota: “Nos queda ese saborcillo agridulce de querer un poquito más, pero igualmente estamos bastante contentos. No éramos cabezas de serie y, por momentos, veíamos que teníamos opciones.” En la eliminatoria por eludir el descenso directo, el Real Zaragoza CT 1907 ha superado al Campus Tenis Club de Granada 4-1 y jugará la promoción contra el Subcampeón de Segunda Categoría, el CT Reus Monterols de Tarragona próximamente.

articles.title: Alcaraz no tiene techo ante De Miñaur y conquista el título de Viena
articles.standfirst: El murciano suma su vigésimo octavo entorchado como profesional, segundo a cubierto
articles.summary: El murciano suma su vigésimo octavo entorchado como profesional, segundo a cubierto
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz ha dado un golpe sobre la mesa en el momento justo. Cuando quedan por disputarse el Masters 1000 de París, las ATP Finals de Turín y la fase final de la Copa Davis de Bolonia, el murciano ha logrado este domingo su segundo torneo en superficie dura bajo techo, las mismas condiciones que se encontrará en lo que le resta de temporada. En 2025, estrenó su palmarés a cubierto en el Open 500 de Rotterdam ante Alex de Miñaur. El australiano ha vuelto a ser la víctima, con un tanteo de 6-1 y 6-4. La táctica del parabrisas, que le valió para derrotar a Alexander Zverev en las semifinales, no le ha hecho ni cosquillas a Alcaraz. Y es que Alex es, junto a Karen Khachanov, la mayor víctima del pupilo de Samuel López (7-0). La tiranía es aún mayor con rivales 'aussies': 15-0. Carlitos suma el vigésimo octavo entorchado como profesional y el cuarto del presente curso, a pesar de haberse perdido más de cuatro meses de competición por la lesión en la muñeca derecha. Es el undécimo certamen de 500 que conquista y alarga su racha de imbatibilidad en la categoría hasta un 26-0. Es el tercer español que levanta el trofeo de Viena desde 1974. Antes lo consiguieron Feliciano López (2004) y David Ferrer (2015). Lo de Alcaraz en la final fue un acoso y derribo desde el primer punto. Rompió el saque de su adversario en el juego inicial. En 14 minutos, el resultado era ya de 3-0. "Las finales están para ganarlas", suele repetir. Ha decantado a su favor 28 de las 37 disputadas. Adolfo Gutiérrez, el entrenador español de De Miñaur, le decía "sigue así, buena actitud esa". El jugador natural de Sidney es de los que no se rinde. Necesitó 26 minutos para estrenar su casillero, pero lo celebró a lo grande porque se había librado del rosco. Por segunda vez en la semana, la anterior fue en los cuartos con Tommy Paul, el campeón de siete grandes no encajó un solo break. Y eso es un mundo en cuanto a confianza para él. Hasta tres veces se quedó con el servicio de su adversario en el primer set. La predisposición de Alex es tan defensiva que no llegaba a ninguna de las dejadas que le proponía su repetido verdugo. Aguantó las embestidas hasta el décimo asalto de la segunda manga. Alcaraz gana con mangas, sin mangas, con pelo, sin pelo y también con bigote. Ahora va a por París, uno de los tres Masters 1000 que le faltan junto a Canadá y Shanghái. Herwig Straka, director del torneo de ATP Viena, dijo en 2023 que el tenista español era demasiado caro. Debería saber ya que verle en directo siempre resulta barato a los ojos del espectador. Carlitos, habitualmente fatigado física y mentalmente a estas alturas de calendario, llega esta vez levitando a la parte final por el forzoso parón de la primavera a causa de la muñeca. Mientras todos sus rivales directos están con la lengua fuera, él pide más tenis. La invitación en Viena se ha saldado con triunfo. La victoria del murciano es un favor directo a su compatriota Rafa Jódar de cara a sus opciones de estar en la cita de maestros reservada a los ocho mejores del año. El madrileño iniciará el TMS parisino a tan sólo un punto de De Miñaur en la Race 2026.

articles.title: Alcaraz ya es el tercer español con más títulos en la Era Open
articles.standfirst: Suma 28, uno más que Ferrer, y sólo tiene por delante a Nadal (92) y Orantes (34)
articles.summary: Suma 28, uno más que Ferrer, y sólo tiene por delante a Nadal (92) y Orantes (34)
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz, con apenas 23 años y 180 días, ha conquistado este domingo en Viena el vigésimo octavo trofeo de su carrera en el circuito profesional de la ATP. Eso le convierte en el tercer español en solitario más laureado de la Era Open. Supera a David Ferrer, el actual seleccionador de la Copa Davis. Por delante de él ya sólo restan Rafael Nadal (92) y Manuel Orantes (34). El pupilo de Samuel López, que suma su cuarto entorchado de un curso en el que se perdió más de cuatro meses de competición por la muñeca, tiene el honor de sumar el entorchado 472 de la Armada masculina desde 1968. Entre los jugadores en activo, sólo Novak Djokovic (101) y Jannik Sinner (30) han ganado más que Carlitos. De hecho, el título del murciano le permite distanciar en dos a Alexander Zverev, flamante número 1 del mundo a partir del lunes 2 de noviembre. El tenis masculino español acumula nueve entorchados esta campaña con los cuatro de Alcaraz (Open de Australia, Doha, Tokio y Viena), los tres de Alejandro Davidovich (Mallorca, Chengdu, Shanghái) y los logrados por Rafa Jódar (Marrakech) y Dani Mérida (Umag).

articles.title: ¿Cuánto dinero gana Alcaraz por el título en el torneo de Viena?
articles.standfirst: El tenista de El Palmar se lleva un talón de 523.306 euros y 500 puntos más a su casillero
articles.summary: El tenista de El Palmar se lleva un talón de 523.306 euros y 500 puntos más a su casillero
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz ha conquistado este domingo en Viena el cuarto título de la temporada y el vigésimo octavo de su carrera con sólo 23 años. El murciano ha derrotado en la final al australiano Alex de Miñaur, que es, junto a Karen Khachanov, la mayor víctima de Carlitos en el circuito profesional. Alcaraz se lleva de tierras austriacas un premio en metálico que asciende a 523.305 euros y 500 puntos para su casillero. A lo larga de su carrera aglutina un total de casi 60 millones de euros en ganancias en la pista, en concreto 59.741.410 euros. El pupilo de Samuel López es sexto en ese ranking histórico, por detrás de Novak Djokovic, Rafael Nadal, Roger Federer, Alexander Zverev y Jannik Sinner. Por su parte, De Miñaur se conforma con 281.540 euros, que corresponde al finalista, además de 330 puntos que le han asegurado el bonus de algo más de un millón de dólares por ser el mejor tenista en torneos de categoría 500 del curso. El australiano suma 1.610 puntos por los 1.550 de Alcaraz, segundo. La bonificación para el fenómeno de El Palmar es de 512.000 dólares. Hay una reducción del 15 por ciento por no haber jugado en Queen's.

articles.summary: El murciano se deshace en elogios hace su equipo, que le empujan a mejorar cada día
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz, de 23 años, ha levantado este domingo el título de Viena, apenas el segundo de su carrera en superficie dura bajo techo. El murciano lo ha celebrado a lo grande abrazándose a los miembros de su banquillo. "La semana de Álex ha sido increíble y siempre estás mejorando. Nos quedan un par de torneos y te deseo lo mejor. Otra gran momento para mí y para mi equipo. Hemos pasado buen tiempo juntos dentro y, sobre todo, fuera. No esperaba jugar aquí y es la mejor decisión que hemos tomado", se sinceraba el vencedor en la ceremonia de premiación. Alex de Miñaur se dirigía así Carlos: "Buen trabajo. Es bonito que estés de vuelta en el circuito, pero es muy frustrante jugar contra ti. Es uno de los mejores tipos del circuito y te felicito por una gran semana". La organización proyectó un vídeo con los mejores momentos de Carlitos en Viena. Sin tiempo de celebración, el campeón hará las maletas dirección a París para disputar el último Masters 1000 del curso. Debutará con el ganador del partido entre Jiri Lehecka y Alex Michelsen.

articles.title: Carlos Alcaraz: Spaniard seals Erste Bank Open victory in Vienna as he defeats Alex de Minaur
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz picks up his fourth title of 2026 with 6-1 6-4 victory; world No 3 defeats Alex de Minaur for seventh match in a row; watch the ATP Paris Masters live on Sky Sports from Monday
articles.body:
The Spaniard, who missed five months of the year with a wrist issue, powered to a 6-1 6-4 win against world No 10 Minaur in the indoor hard-court event.

World No 3 Alcaraz delivered a high-quality, 97-minute display to overwhelm De Minaur and secure the title without dropping a set across his five matches.

The 23-year-old arrived in Vienna following titles in Doha and Tokyo ‌and completed a perfect 16-0 record at ATP 500 events in ​2026 with another dominant week.

"My team and I know pretty well Alex de Minaur's level," Alcaraz said. "His style is really dangerous. Really flat balls that slip a lot through the court really low. It's really difficult to increase the power that I want to in every shot and every ball.

"He's really fast, so you have to earn every point. You might hit a winner against everybody, except him. I had to be really focused on that, so we knew I had to start the match really focused, increasing my speed, my pace in every shot.

"I tried to be aggressive and show him that if he wants to win, he has to play better [than me], more aggressive, more solid, and be smarter than me.

"I'm just really happy that at the end I found my way, played great, and obviously it has been a really emotional and amazing week for me.

"I learned a lot, to keep going forward, step by step, playing on indoor courts, and trying to gain more confidence playing on this surface."

Alcaraz seized control from the ​opening stages, breaking De Minaur's serve ⁠in the first game and ⁠quickly establishing a double-break advantage as the Australian struggled to deal with his intensity.

The seven-time Grand Slam champion raced through the opening, repeatedly punishing short balls ‌and forcing errors from De Minaur.

Although De Minaur put up greater resistance in the second set and kept pace for long spells, Alcaraz closed out victory and secured his seventh ​consecutive win over his opponent.

Alcaraz, who has already qualified for the season-ending ATP Finals in Turin, will head ​to next week's Paris Masters brimming with confidence.

He takes on Jiri Lehecka or Alex Michelsen in his first match.

De Minaur, meanwhile, will turn ​his attention to Paris as he continues his ​push to qualify for the ATP Finals for a third consecutive year.

Vacherot rallies to beat Lehecka to win Swiss Indoors and clinch a second career title

Valentin Vacherot clinched his second career title after beating Jiri Lehecka 2-6 6-3 6-3 in the Swiss Indoors final on Sunday.

The unseeded Vacherot's other title came at the Shanghai Masters last year, when the player from Monaco came through the qualifying rounds.

He sealed victory this time when Lehecka's two-handed backhand landed just out. The eighth-seeded Czech player was seeking his first title of the year.

Vacherot waved his racket to the fans in Basel as he celebrated his win.

articles.standfirst: El técnico regresará al circuito con un ilusionante proyecto al lado del mejor tenista americano
articles.summary: El técnico regresará al circuito con un ilusionante proyecto al lado del mejor tenista americano
articles.body: Juan Carlos Ferrero, a sus 46 años, regresará el año que viene al circuito al lado del zurdo Ben Shelton. Según ha adelantado 'The Times' y ha podido confirmar MARCA, el estadounidense es el elegido por el preparador español para volver al circuito. Después de la filtración, ha llegado la confirmación oficial por parte de las dos partes en las redes sociales. "Una gran incorporación la de Ferrero a mi equipo. Con muchas ganas de trabajar juntos en la pretemporada", decía Shelton. Shelton, de 24 años, ocupa el cuarto puesto del ranking ATP y esta campaña fue verdugo de Carlos Alcaraz en los cuartos del US Open. Alcanzó su primera final de Grand Slam con Alexander Zverev. Ferrero se une a un equipo en el que también figura Bryan Shelton, padre del número 1 del tenis americano. Ambos coincidirán por primera vez en las ATP Finals de Turín (15 al 22). "Ben tiene un talento y un potencial extraordinario y me siento muy contento de unirme a Bryan y al resto del equipo en este nuevo capítulo", comunicaba Juan Carlos. Juanqui acudirá el primer fin de semana de la competición como invitado en la cena de gala para los números 1 de la historia del tenis. Shelton se ha clasificado por segunda campaña seguida para la cita de maestros. Será la tercera experiencia de Ferrero en los banquillos tras la vivida al lado de Alexander Zverev y Alcaraz.

articles.title: How Harriet Dart revived career under former Wimbledon champion Marion Bartoli
articles.summary: Britain's Harriet Dart knows people doubted whether she would ever win a WTA title, but says the belief of her coach Marion Bartoli helped achieve the best week of her career.
articles.body:
In the hour following her first WTA title win, Britain's Harriet Dart had little time to respond to the stream of congratulatory messages flashing up on her phone.

Most pressing was making a call to her proud parents, Nick and Susie, who had been watching the final with friends at their local tennis club in north London, and her sister Phoebe.

The next person she spoke to was 2013 Wimbledon champion Marion Bartoli.

Dart has been coached by the French former world number seven since the start of the season on a part-time basis, and she credits Bartoli for helping her achieve what some thought was beyond her.

On Sunday, with Bartoli watching from home, the world number 115 won the Guangzhou Open in China by beating rising Austrian teenager Lilli Tagger.

"It's been quite incredible to work with Marion, and I was really fortunate she was open to working with me," Dart, 30, told BBC Sport in a video call from Guangzhou.

"I'm obviously at a very different stage of my career to someone who is, say, 20. But I still feel I have a lot to improve and there are gains to be made.

"She really believes in me - that means the world to me. Seeing a Grand Slam champion having that belief has made me believe a lot more in myself."

Britain's Dart wins first WTA title in 'wild week'

When Dart started working with Bartoli, she was ranked outside the top 160. The pair live close to each other in Dubai and spend training blocks together there when Dart is not on the road.

Dart and Bartoli, who has a young family, are not travelling full-time together on tour, but there have been opportunities for them to work on the ground, particularly during this year's Grand Slam tournaments.

Dart says 42-year-old Bartoli still hitting the ball "really well" in practice is another benefit of the partnership.

In Guangzhou, Dart was accompanied by her fitness trainer Dario Gonfiantini and boyfriend Stephen Falck. Without her coach, Dart had to largely rely on figuring things out herself - with the help of Bartoli sending over observational notes.

Dart is projected to rise to 83rd on Monday after lifting the Guangzhou trophy to cap a stunning second half of the season.

Dart has won 19 of her 24 tour-level matches on the hard courts since Wimbledon, taking her overall record on the WTA Tour this season to 23 victories from 34 matches - the highest winning percentage of her career.

"More than anything, Marion is just a great person. She cares about me as a person first and foremost, as well as improving me as a tennis player, of course," Dart said.

"It's been invaluable and amazing for her to share her experiences to make me better.

"I've learned a lot from her and look forward to continuing to learn more. I hope we will be able to spend more weeks together next year."

Dart reached a career high of 70th in the world in 2024, having made the Wimbledon third round and US Open second round, but has languished outside the top 100 for most of the past two seasons.

During this period there have been clear vulnerabilities with her game, with opponents learning they could take advantage of a slow second serve that tended to produce double faults.

There have also been questions about her on-court mentality and whether she could handle the pressure moments.

In Guangzhou, she answered those doubts with a series of gutsy wins where she needed to fight back from behind.

"She's always had a fantastic work ethic and has always set the bar high with her professionalism," Anne Keothavong, Britain's women's team captain, told BBC Sport.

"But there is certainly more belief and confidence now. She's in a very good place.

"She's been grinding away on the tour for a long time and it's great to see someone who has put in a lot of time to succeed and win a big title."

Keothavong named Dart in her squad for September's Billie Jean King Cup Finals and although she did not select Dart to play in the tie, she was impressed by her ball-striking during practice.

Taking that level back on tour has helped Dart continue what has been an encouraging few weeks for British women in the Asian hard-court swing.

Sonay Kartal reached the final of a WTA 1000 event in Wuhan, Katie Boulter made the semi-finals at a WTA 250 in Osaka and now Dart has won her maiden title at WTA 250 level.

Last week, teenager Hannah Klugman won the biggest title of her career at the Wrexham Open - a W100 event on the second-tier Challenger tour.

"The way they're all performing towards the end of the season - at whatever level - has been impressive," added Keothavong.

"It's not easy at this time of the season because there has been a lot of tennis played, but they've all capitalised and risen to the occasion.

"It's great reward for all their hard work and is encouraging for British tennis."

articles.title: "Always worry about": Steffi Graf and Andre Agassi's parenting decision kept their two children away from the pressure of tennis stardom
articles.summary: Growing up with two of the greatest tennis players in history could easily make professional sports feel like a family tradition.
articles.body: Growing up with two of the greatest tennis players in history could easily make professional sports feel like a family tradition. But Steffi Graf and Andre Agassi had a different vision for their children. Despite building legendary careers and collecting some of tennis' biggest honours, the couple never expected their son, Jaden, and daughter, Jaz, to follow in their footsteps. Instead, they allowed both children to discover their own interests, build separate identities and enjoy childhood without the pressure of living up to their famous surname.Meet Steffi Graf and Andre Agassi's children, Jaden and JazGraf and Agassi married in October 2001, shortly before welcoming their first child. Their son, Jaden Gil Agassi, was born on October 26, 2001. Two years later, on October 3, 2003, they welcomed their daughter, Jaz Elle Agassi.Although their parents spent decades competing at the highest level, the children grew up largely away from public attention.Agassi's own childhood played an important role in shaping his parenting approach. In his autobiography, Open, he described the intense pressure his father placed on him to become a successful tennis player.“My father yells everything twice, sometimes three times, sometimes 10,” he wrote. “Harder, he says, harder. Hit earlier. Damn it Andre, hit earlier, Crowd the ball, crowd the ball.”Having experienced that demanding environment himself, Agassi wanted something different for his children. Graf also made it clear that they were free to choose their own interests.“We never really introduced tennis so much into their lives. They’ve chosen other things,” the mom of two shared.Why Jaden and Jaz Agassi never pursued professional tennisJaden found his passion in baseball rather than tennis. He joined the University of Southern California in 2019 and played college baseball before gaining experience with summer league teams. In 2025, he also represented Team Germany in the World Baseball Classic Qualifiers.His ambition is to build a sporting identity separate from his parents' achievements.“Agassi is a very tennis last name, of course,” Jaden told WKBN News in June 2024. “The goal is to try to make it a baseball one.”Jaz, meanwhile, has explored dancing and horseback riding. She also enjoys outdoor activities, including snowboarding. Unlike her brother, she keeps much of her personal life away from public attention.Agassi has also spoken openly about protecting his children's freedom to choose their own paths.“The idea that a parent would attach a child’s right to be loved in this world based on their performance is a tragedy,” he explained in a 2024 conversation with USA Today. “What somebody needs to do to be pro at 16 years old is crazy, right?”He once described tennis as an unusual sport and explained why he and Graf avoided pushing their children towards it.“It’s a weird sport,” Andre told Fox Sports. “We don’t see too many second-generation players. For us, it’s about raising our children in a way we can share in their life and not always worry about their life.”For the tennis legends, their children's happiness matters far more than another championship trophy.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Leander Paes to run for AITA vice-prez
articles.summary: PUNE: In a move filled with surprise and intrigue, Leander Paes has decided to run for the lone vice-president's post in the All India Tennis Association
articles.body: PUNE: In a move filled with surprise and intrigue, Leander Paes has decided to run for the lone vice-president's post in the All India Tennis Association (AITA) elections, scheduled for Nov. 27.The 18-time Grand Slam winner's candidature was revealed by Chintan Parikh, AITA's interim president, in a press release on Sunday."Parikh will contest for president and Paes for vice-president. Both of them will be supported by a capable team comprising an honorary secretary, treasurer, two joint secretaries and other executive committee members. These names will be decided in the next few days," the press release said.Parikh said his partnership with Paes, who is the president of the Bengal Tennis Association, was finalised after a meeting between the two in Kolkata on Friday.As per the National Sports Governance Act, 2025, a candidate must have completed at least one term as an office-bearer in a state association or on the executive committee of the national body to be eligible to run for president. Paes was elected to the BTA's top job last November.Despite being the only Olympic medallist on the Sportsperson of Outstanding Merit (SOM) roster, he chose not to contest the AITA presidency. articles.title: Shelton habla de Ferrero desde París: "Es uno de los mejores, fue número 1 y puede marcar la diferencia"
articles.standfirst: El estadounidense se deshace en elogios hacia el entrenador español
articles.summary: El estadounidense se deshace en elogios hacia el entrenador español
articles.body: Ben Shelton ha reaccionado desde París a la noticia del fichaje de Juan Carlos Ferrero para su banquillo de cara a la próxima temporada. El número cuatro mundial, que es el tercer cabeza de serie del cuadro del último Masters 1000 del curso, habla ya abiertamente del que será su nuevo técnico para la temporada 2027. El estadounidense da las razones por las que ha apostado por Ferrero, que se unirá a un equipo en el que está ya su padre Bryan: "Es uno de los mejores técnicos del mundo, fue número 1 como jugador y hay mucha experiencia y conocimiento que puede aportarme. Puede marcar las diferencias en mi carrera". Shelton, exento de la ronda inicial en el TMS de París, se las verá con el ganador del partido entre Cameron Norrie y Matteo Arnaldi. Desde que alcanzó la final del US Open, sólo ha ganado dos partidos. Uno a Daniel Altmaier, en Shanghái, y otro a Aleksandar Kovacevic, en Basilea. articles.title: 8 Tennis Players Retire in October 2026
articles.summary: October was one of the busiest months of tennis farewells. Eight prominent tennis players retired from the sport, including a three-time Grand Slam champion....
articles.body:
October was one of the busiest months of tennis farewells. Eight prominent tennis players retired from the sport, including a three-time Grand Slam champion. On that note, we have the complete list.

Of the eight names on this list, Ana Bogdan's retirement was probably the most low-key. Bogdan last featured in February 2026 at the Transylvania Open in her home country. The former WTA World No. 39 has since updated her official Instagram profile , which now reads "Former Professional Tennis Player."

Kei Nishikori's retirement was well documented . It was a matter of when and not if the former US Open finalist would bow out in 2026. And the injury-prone Japanese star hung up his racket following a first-round defeat to Frances Tiafoe at the Japan Open. Among his most significant accolades, Nishikori won 12 ATP titles and defeated Rafael Nadal to clinch a Bronze Medal at the 2016 Olympics in Rio.

Gael Monfils was set to retire before the end of the 2026 season, but his decision to retire in the past caught many by surprise. The Frenchman endured double heartbreak in the past month. His marriage to WTA star Elina Svitolina ended following the couple's announcement of their separation . Monfils then decided to retire from tennis earlier than planned because of the split . He withdrew from all mandatory anti-doping protocols and submitted his name to the International Integrity Agency (ITIA) retirement list.

Stan Wawrinka retired from tennis after a first-round defeat to Jiri Lehecka at the Swiss Indoors. Wawrinka received a fitting farewell in Basel in front of a packed home crowd. The 41-year-old won 16 Tour-level titles, including three Grand Slams. He partnered Roger Federer to win a gold medal at the 2008 Beijing Olympics, and the duo was instrumental in helping Switzerland win its first Davis Cup title in 2014.

A third home farewell took place at the ATP 250 in Brussels, where Belgium's David Goffin called time on his career . Goffin is the first and thus far only Belgian male player to reach the world's Top 10. He won 6 ATP titles and was a runner-up at the 2017 ATP Finals.

Former ATP Top 100 player Gastao Elias also retired on home soil. The 35-year-old picked the Lisbon Challenger as the final tournament of his career, and he was granted that opportunity. Elias fell to a straight-sets defeat in the first round and shortly after gave a tearful retirement speech .

The last home farewell in this list took place in Almaty, where one of the best Kazakhstani tennis players retired at the ATP 250 event. Mikhail Kukushkin lost to Stefanos Tsitsipas in the Round of 16 and officially retired. Kukushkin won his only Tour-level title at the 2010 St. Petersburg Open

Alicia Smith confirmed her retirement on Instagram . In an emotional post, Smith noted that she was stepping away from professional tennis after a 15-year career. The 30-year-old Australian mostly competed in the lower leagues and won six ITF doubles titles.

articles.title: Alexander Zverev becomes deserved world number one but sense of discomfort remains
articles.summary: Alexander Zverev has been the best player in the world in men's tennis this year - but a sense of discomfort remains.
articles.body:
Before this year, Alexander Zverev was, for many, the best male player never to have won a Grand Slam.

He will end 2026 as a two-time major champion and deserved world number one.

The 29-year-old has become the oldest man in more than 50 years to become world number one for the first time, with victories at the French Open and US Open providing the springboard.

Diagnosed with type 1 diabetes aged four, his overdue Grand Slam breakthrough was a reward for persistence and intense hard work.

However, the new standard-bearer for men's tennis has been accused of physical abuse by two former partners, and been the subject of a major independent investigation by the sport.

How 10 days with Nadal changed on-court approach

At the start of this year, Zverev was already an Olympic champion, two-time winner of the season-ending ATP Finals and a former world number two who had appeared in three Grand Slam finals.

The most excruciating of those was the 2020 US Open final, in which he led Dominic Thiem by two sets to love but lost in a fifth-set tie-break after serving two double faults as his opponent began to cramp.

The inability to play with the same freedom and attacking intent that is often on show in big matches on the ATP Tour had become a perennial problem.

This year would be different, he promised himself. He would hit the ball with more speed, take greater risk and employ more variety in rallies.

The impetus stemmed from the 10 days he spent with Rafael and Toni Nadal in Mallorca in July 2025.

"I wanted to see and then hear a new vision of what tennis in their mind looks like - and how my tennis, in their mind, looks like," Zverev explained.

"Rafa, for example, played against me for 10 years. So now, as a spectator and also as an opponent, he can probably give you the best advice anybody can, because he knows what it's like to be on the court with me."

There were still moments of extreme anxiety, including cramping in June's French Open final against Flavio Cobolli.

But this time Zverev made no mistake in the deciding set, winning it 6-1 to claim his long-awaited first major trophy.

Zverev's on-court success is a family affair. His father, Alex Sr, has been a near-constant presence in the coaching box, while older brother Mischa has joined him since his retirement from playing.

That particular relationship has come full circle, as Zverev was once a toddler sitting by the side of the court as Mischa practised with Andy Murray as a junior.

Zverev has said his relationship with his father works so well as they spend "zero time together" off court.

"The big difference with my parents is that they never forced me to do anything," Zverev once recalled.

"They wanted me to play different sports so they didn't have to coach me. They always told me 'why don't you play football, or field hockey?' as that was the sport I loved.

"They are very smart. They've been through it. They've been tennis players themselves."

Not only is Zverev now the French and US Open champion , but he was also runner-up at Wimbledon, where he played his best tennis of the year.

He was aggressive and daring in a four-set defeat by Jannik Sinner on Centre Court, and will need to take a leaf out of the same book in future meetings with both the Italian and Carlos Alcaraz.

The German has lost 10 matches in a row to Sinner, and if he and Alcaraz are fit for the start of next season, Zverev's challenge will be to make 2027 a three-way rivalry for the major titles.

Zverev has previously been the subject of serious allegations.

In October 2020, his ex-partner Olga Sharypova accused him of physical violence and controlling behaviour.

Zverev maintained his innocence from the start and described the allegations as baseless.

There were no legal proceedings, but the ATP Tour opened a major investigation that was carried out by third-party investigators.

It found "insufficient evidence to substantiate published allegations of abuse".

"Based on a lack of reliable evidence and eyewitness reports, in addition to conflicting statements by Sharypova, Zverev and other interviewees, the investigation was unable to substantiate the allegations of abuse," the ATP said in January 2023.

A director of safeguarding was subsequently appointed, and this year a new safeguarding programme was launched to introduce a "clear, global framework for preventing and responding to abuse, including cases of harassment, bullying, domestic violence and other forms of misconduct".

In October 2023, Zverev was issued with a penalty order and fined 450,000 euros (£392,000) by a German court for bodily harm against another ex-girlfriend, Brenda Patea.

Zverev denied the claims and contested the order, with a public trial taking place in Berlin in May 2024.

A week into the process, the court terminated the proceedings before a verdict could be reached, and told the BBC there had been a settlement between Zverev and Patea.

"The decision is not a verdict and it is not a decision about guilt or innocence," the court said.

"One decisive factor for the court decision was that the witness [Zverev's ex-partner] has expressed her wish to end the trial."

Zverev reached the French Open final on the day the settlement was announced. Having spoken earlier in the tournament about the trial being a chance to prove his innocence, he was asked whether he had any regrets about settling before that was possible.

"That's what dropping the case is. That is innocence," he argued.

"They're not going to drop the case if you're guilty at the end of the day. I don't know what translations you have, but that's what it means.

"Done. We move on. I never ever want to hear another question about the subject again. That goes out to everybody."

Patea has not publicly commented on the settlement.

Zverev was heckled by spectators in 2025 at the Australian Open and Munich Open over the allegations.

In 2022, he was given an eight-week suspended ban by the ATP Tour after being found guilty of a 'major offence' for smashing his racquet into the umpire's chair four times after losing a doubles match at the Mexican Open.

Zverev, who was thrown out of the tournament in Acapulco for unsportsmanlike behaviour, was incensed by a line call that went against him and partner Marcelo Melo in a deciding tie-break.

He swore at umpire Alessandro Germani and accused him of destroying the whole match. One of his four angry swipes at the chair nearly caught the umpire on the foot.

Zverev later apologised and said it was "difficult to put into words" how much he regretted his behaviour.

The ban was never imposed, as Zverev avoided being fined for 'disrespectful or aggressive behaviour, or verbal or physical abuse' in the 12 months following the incident.

articles.title: Katie Boulter wins in Hong Kong despite incident that 'got under my skin' during match versus Viktorija Golubic
articles.summary: Katie Boulter was twice broken when serving for the match in the second set after British No 1 says incident "got under my skin"; the world No 49 went on to beat Viktorija Golubic 6-2 7-6; watch the ATP Paris Masters live on Sky Sports from Monday November 2
articles.body:
Boulter was twice broken when serving for the match in the second set, having complained to the umpire when up 5-2 after a point was not replayed despite her being distracted by a noise from outside the court.

She ultimately triumphed in a tiebreak to take the match 6-2 7-6 (7-2), clinching a fourth win in five following on from reaching the semi-finals in Japan Open last month that saw her reclaim top spot from Sonay Kartal as British No 1.

Boulter, ranked 49th in the world and seeded eighth at the tournament, had got the better of Golubic in Osaka two weeks ago and repeated the feat in her Hong Kong opener.

She was broken early on by the Swiss but hit back to win eight games in a row to take the first set and control the second.

A superb passing winner at the net helped Boulter move 4-1 up before she squandered match point on Golubic's serve and was then broken twice, but the 30-year-old held her nerve to first force a tiebreak and then take it to reach the last 16, where she'll face American Claire Liu.

"It was interesting," Boulter said of her second-set wobble. "I was playing some really good tennis. I feel like I should have closed it out but a couple of things happened.

"There was a little bit of interesting judgement which got under my skin a little bit and, usually, I'm pretty good at batting it off but I was a little tired.

"It's end of season and it seemed to get to me but lesson learned, I managed to get over the line."

Venus losing streak extends to 17 singles matches

Venus Williams failed to break her losing streak in singles during 2026, with the seven-time Grand Slam champion falling to another defeat in the Hong Kong Open.

Williams was beaten by fellow American Mary Stoiana 6-2 6-3 in the opening round.

The 46-year-old last won a singles match on the WTA Tour in July 2025 and has lost her last 17 encounters.

The longest overall losing streak in WTA history belongs to Madeleine Pegel, who lost 29 consecutive matches between 1968 and 1972.

articles.body:
Katie Boulter said it was "lesson learned" as she overcame an incident that "got under my skin" to reach the last 16 of the Hong Kong Open.

The British number one was broken by Viktorija Golubic when serving for the match at 5-2 up in the second set.

During the game, Boulter complained to the umpire after a point was not replayed for an audible noise from outside causing a distraction.

An unsettled Boulter also lost her next service game before the world number 49 came through a tie-break to take a 6-2 7-6 (7-2) victory.

"It was interesting," said Boulter, who was the losing finalist at the Hong Kong Open in 2024.

"I was playing some really good tennis. I feel like I should have closed it out but a couple of things happened.

"There was a little bit of interesting judgement which got under my skin a little bit and, usually, I'm pretty good at batting it off but I was a little tired.

"It's end of season and it seemed to get to me but lesson learned, I managed to get over the line."

Boulter, who beat world number 89 Golubic in dominant fashion when reaching the semi-finals at the Japan Open last month, will play American Claire Liu in the next round.

How Dart revived career with help of Wimbledon champion

Williams loses again - to opponent 28 years younger

Meanwhile, Venus Williams suffered a 17th consecutive singles defeat as she was beaten by fellow American Mary Stoiana in the first round in Hong Kong.

The 46-year-old, who is 597th in the women's rankings, lost 6-2 6-3 to 23-year-old Stoiana, who is ranked 113th.

Williams - a seven-time Grand Slam singles champion - has not won a singles match since July 2025 and relies on wildcards to play WTA tournaments.

articles.body: Alexander Zverev has finally reached the summit of men's tennis, becoming the world No. 1 for the first time in his career on Monday and setting a remarkable record in the process. The 29-year-old German became the oldest player in 52 years to reach the top of the ATP rankings for the first time, ending a wait that had stretched across several seasons.Zverev is only the 30th player to occupy the top spot since the ATP rankings were introduced. He also becomes just the second German man to achieve the distinction in singles, joining compatriot and former world No. 1 Boris Becker.His rise to the top comes after a remarkable season in which he captured two Grand Slam titles, winning the French Open in June with a victory over Flavio Cobolli before defeating Ben Shelton to lift the US Open trophy at Flushing Meadows in September.Those triumphs helped silence years of criticism over his inability to convert his talent into major titles. Zverev had often been described as the 'greatest player never to win a Grand Slam' before finally delivering on the biggest stages.Zverev's long wait finally endsThe German's achievement is particularly significant given his age. He is the oldest first-time world No. 1 since John Newcombe, who reached the summit at the age of 30 in 1974.Zverev had previously climbed to No. 2 more than four years ago but had been unable to take the final step. Reflecting on his long journey to the top, he said: "I had to wait. But sometimes you've got to wait for the best things in life. I'm super happy, super thrilled."The two Grand Slam crowns have been part of an outstanding season for Zverev, who also reached the Wimbledon final, losing to Jannik Sinner, and the Australian Open semifinals.He has compiled a 65-17 win-loss record this year and added to an already impressive collection of trophies that includes two ATP Finals titles, an Olympic singles gold medal and seven Masters 1000 titles.Sinner slips as Zverev takes overZverev's elevation to the top has also brought an end to Sinner's reign as world No. 1. articles.title: Harriet Dart: Former Wimbledon champion Marion Bartoli on pushing Brit 'beyond her limits' after maiden WTA title
articles.summary: Former Wimbledon champion and Sky Sports analyst Marion Bartoli speaks about mentoring Harriet Dart and why she thinks the Brit can break the top 30 in the world; You can watch the ATP Paris Masters live on Sky Sports all this week
articles.body:
Dart, playing in her first Tour-level final, edged a thrilling match against 18-year-old Lilli Tagger from Austria 4-6 6-3 6-4 .

The 30-year-old from Hampstead returned back into the top 100 of the WTA rankings and has a strong chance of automatic qualification into the main draw of the Australian Open, which runs from January 11-31.

Bartoli, who started working with Dart on a part-time basis since the start of the year, discussed her coaching philosophy and why she thought it was only a matter of time before the Brit would go on and make her mark.

Speaking to Sky Sports , the 2013 Wimbledon winner said: "I thought Harriet could do extremely well after the US open because everything we were working on in her game was starting to come to life more and more.

"Now, to tell you she could win a title, it was not my obsession. For me, as a coach, that's not how I function. Everything has to follow a certain process of improvements. Once those improvements are made, that's when the results start to come. That's my whole philosophy behind my coaching system.

"We had a very strong week of training in Dubai, and when I hugged her at the end of her last practice with me before she left for Osaka, I told her: 'You are playing amazing tennis, believe in yourself and keep fighting!'

"She did exactly that and so much more."

Bartoli began dissecting Dart's game with the Brit ranked outside the top 160 at the time.

"When she contacted me earlier this year to start a collaboration, I knew exactly what I would like her to change and improve. The problem we were both facing is the lack of time we could actually properly spend together to work on her game," said the former French Open semi-finalist and world No 7.

"We started to properly do that only when we were in Florida before Cincinnati, and since then, it has been incredibly satisfying to see how quickly Harriet has been improving, taking things on board, committed fully to them and applying them in matches.

"Seeing her now regularly serving several aces per match, moving forward, taking the ball early and going to an open stance more often, and charging the net.

"She won the Guangzhou tournament on a serve winner... it says a lot!"

Dart has won 19 of her 24 tour-level matches on the hard courts since Wimbledon with Bartoli admitting the Billie Jean King Cup regular is always pushing herself beyond her limits.

"She is an incredible fast learner once you have her trust," revealed Bartoli. "There is never a problem to explain my theories and my thoughts behind a change I am asking her to do.

"She is extremely coachable and more importantly she is always giving 100 per cent in practice, which is for me a massive quality.

"I pushed her beyond her limits in practice, but she equally pushed herself beyond her own limits."

Bartoli felt a release of emotion on Sunday, and with Dart now up to world No 83 and British No 3, the Frenchwoman is certain there is more to come.

"I am feeling incredibly proud of her after her win," Bartoli said. "The week she had, the number of matches she had to win in three sets is a true testimony to the relentless competitor she is.

"I cried when she won on a serve winner because I know how much time we have spent on that shot, and for her to finish on a match point like that speaks volumes.

"The future will be really bright for Harriet. We are just getting started because there is a lot I still want to add to her game.

It's been a successful time for British women's tennis with Sonay Kartal reaching the final of a WTA 1000 event in Wuhan, Katie Boulter making the semi-finals at a WTA 250 in Osaka, and now Dart sealing her maiden title at WTA 250 level.

Teenager Hannah Klugman also won the biggest title of her career at the Wrexham Open - a W100 event on the second-tier Challenger tour.

articles.summary: El madrileño se afianza en las posiciones de acceso directo a las ATP Finals de Turín
articles.body: Rafa Jódar depende de sí mismo para acompañar a Carlos Alcaraz en las ATP Finals de Turín (15 al 22). El madrileño ha estrenado este lunes su condición de 'top10' mundial con su primera victoria en el Masters 1000 de París. Eso le afianza en el noveno puesto de la Race 2026, que le daría el billete directo a la cita de maestros. Alex de Miñaur, su más directo perseguidor, está a 64 puntos. El australiano, octavo cabeza de serie en el TMS galo y por tanto exento de la ronda inicial, necesitará ganar en su estreno para seguir en la carrera. Más rezagados vienen Novak Djokovic, Taylor Fritz, Tommy Paul y Jiri Lehecka, todos ellos con opciones matemáticas. También las tiene Alejandro Davidovich aunque debería levantar el título en París y esperar una carambola de resultados. Djokovic, a sus 39 años, está a 334 puntos de Jódar y tendría que hacer semifinales para adelantar a Jódar. No iba a ser Alejandro Tabilo el que privara a Rafa de seguir soñando con acabar su prime curso como profesional entre los ocho mejores. El chileno, que había cedido los últimos tres precedentes, el último la semana pasada en Basilea, lo hizo una cuarta vez, con un tanteo de 6-2 y 6-3. Y eso que empezó dominando el partido, con un 2-1 y servicio. Pero su repetido verdugo no se descompuso en ningún momento y encadenó cinco juegos para anotarse la manga inicial. La secuencia de asaltos a su favor llegó hasta los seis. Su velocidad y aceleración desmontan a cualquiera. Rafa no regala nada. Así ha sido educado por su padre y entrenador, que responde al mismo nombre y que ha viajado con él toda la temporada. Cuando Tabilo atajó la sangría ya era demasiado tarde para pensar en la remontada. Su impotencia la pagó su raqueta, que acabó por los suelos. Ya son 11 triunfos del madrileño ante zurdos en 14 partidos. El chileno fue capaz de remontar un 3-1 adverso en el segundo set. El saque del noveno favorito del cuadro cerró cualquier tipo de opción a la sorpresa en una central del Plenitude Arena. A Jódar no le frena el cansancio de los 77 duelos acumulados en sus piernas, de los que ha decantado 58 a su favor. En Basilea acabó perdiendo en la segunda ronda con un Valentin Vacherot que se coronó el domingo frente a Lehecka. El tenista del Chamartín espera en la segunda ronda al ganador a Casper Ruud, verdugo Juan Manuel Cerúndolo. Ganó al noruego en el único precedente entre ambos en los cuartos del Masters 1000 de Shanghái. El objetivo de acompañar a Alcaraz en Turín está un poco más cerca. Los dos miembros de la Armada coincidirán después en el equipo español de Copa Davis que buscará levantar la séptima Ensaladera de su historia en Bolonia (24 al 29). "Si quieres ser de los mejores del mundo, tienes que tener un tenis muy completo y sin altibajos en los partidos. Creo que es algo que estoy haciendo bien, en especial en estos últimos torneos del año. Soy todavía joven y quiero seguir mejorando en las próximas campañas", reflexiona Jódar.

articles.title: Dani Mérida se reencuentra con el triunfo ante el argentino Báez
articles.standfirst: El madrileño venía de perder en su debut en Shanghái y en Viena
articles.summary: El madrileño venía de perder en su debut en Shanghái y en Viena
articles.body: Dani Mérida, el 42 del ranking ATP a sus 22 años, sigue con opciones de acabar la temporada con la mejor clasificación de su carrera. Su tope es el puesto 39. El madrileño, que venía de perder en el debut en el Masters 1000 de Shanghái y el Open 500 de Viena, se ha clasificado este lunes para la segunda ronda de París, el último torneo Masters 1000 del curso. Mérida ha dado buena cuenta de Sebastián Báez, por 6-4 y 6-2, en 1 hora y 16 minutos. El argentino se había metido en el cuadro principal como 'lucky loser' de la previa. El español espera ahora al ganador del partido entre Tommy Paul (12) y Holger Rune. Dani pondrá punto y final a una exitosa temporada cuando concluya el TMS de París y no jugará finalmente la semana que viene en Estocolmo. El joven madrileño se ha metido en el 'top100', ha ganado su primer título como profesional en Umag y ha hecho su debut en el equipo español de la Copa Davis en la eliminatoria en tierras chilenas. articles.title: Zverev ya tiene su trofeo de nº1 del mundo
articles.standfirst: El alemán ha recibido el galardón al término de la sesión de día en la pista central del Masters 1000 de París
articles.summary: El alemán ha recibido el galardón al término de la sesión de día en la pista central del Masters 1000 de París
articles.body: Alexander Zverev tenía como uno de sus principales objetivos conseguir el número 1 del ranking ATP. Hoy, lunes 2 de noviembre de 2026, el alemán se ha levantado en la capital francesa como tal, el líder del circuito masculino. Al término de la sesión de día en la Défense Arena de París, la organización le ha hecho entrega del prestigioso galardón, que tan solo han sido capaces de levantar 30 profesionales de la raqueta en la historia. Sascha es el segundo tenista más longevo en conseguirlo con 29 años y 196 días. Solo le supera en edad el estadounidense John Newcombe, que lo logró a los 30 años y 11 días. El segundo alemán desde que Boris Becker estrenara este ranking para los teutones en 1991. Al recibir el trofeo, el cual Zverev no dudó en besar como con cada certamen o distinción que levanta, quiso expresar el honor que sentía como jugador: "Estar en el club del número 1 del mundo con estos grandes campeones es uno de los mayores honores que puedes tener como jugador de tenis. Formar parte de él es una sensación increíblemente especial", adelantaba Sascha en su discurso en la central parisina. El campeón de 26 títulos iniciará su campaña en el último TMS de la temporada, el cual ganó en 2024, ante Lorenzo Musetti. Alexander Zverev ha cumplido en este 2026 los deseos que llevaba anhelando desde que debutara en el circuito profesional en 2013: ser campeón de Grand Slam (lo ha hecho hasta en dos ocasiones, Roland Garros y US Open) y convertirse en número 1. Tras esto, Sascha ha logrado coronarse en todos los tipos de torneos a nivel individual: Grand Slam, medalla de oro olímpica, ATP Finals, Masters 1000, ATP 500 y ATP 250. Se cierra un ciclo que comenzó en 2016, cuando levantó en San Petersburgo, ante Stan Wawrinka, su primer certamen como profesional. Tan solo le falta alzarse con la Copa Davis para, junto a Novak Djokovic, ser los dos únicos tenistas en conseguir todo tipo de títulos. El reto lo tendrá del 24 al 29 de noviembre en la 'Final a 8' de Bolonia con su querida Alemania. Al igual que Carlos Alcaraz en 2022, cuando recibió el trofeo de número 1 en París y el de fin de año en Turín, Zverev repetirá esta escena. El alemán levantará ante el público del Inalpi Arena de Turín la copa que le acredita como número 1 de final de temporada. Las Nitto ATP Finals tendrán lugar del 15 al 22 de este mes.

articles.title: Juan Carlos Ferrero: Ben Shelton appoints Carlos Alcaraz's former coach - will it work?
articles.summary: US Open runner-up Ben Shelton joins forces with Juan Carlos Ferrer, the former coach of Carlos Alcaraz - BBC Sport analyses why the partnership suits both parties.
articles.body:
Ben Shelton's name rarely cropped up when Juan Carlos Ferrero - the former world number one who nurtured Carlos Alcaraz to stardom - teased he was going to coach a new player.

But there are obvious reasons why it suits both parties.

For US Open runner-up Shelton, it is an opportunity to tap into a mind that knows how to win major titles and has the inside track on the world's very best.

Ferrero started working with Alcaraz when he was 15, turning his fellow Spaniard from a "piece of spaghetti" into a seven-time Grand Slam champion.

Alcaraz is seen as the most naturally gifted player on the ATP Tour, having dominated the biggest tournaments alongside Jannik Sinner before their respective injuries this season.

Guiding world number four Shelton is a different assignment.

With explosive power and supreme athleticism, the 24-year-old American already possesses weapons which can inflict serious damage.

The left-hander has been a fixture inside the world's top 20 for the past four seasons and reached his first Grand Slam final in New York two months ago.

However, he has often fallen short against the very best.

Shelton earned the best win of his career against an undercooked Alcaraz in September's US Open quarter-finals, but could not beat new world number one Alexander Zverev in the championship match.

His New York run was underpinned by an improved backhand and better defensive skills, but not being able to execute his damaging forehand in crucial moments proved costly against Zverev.

Shelton has also suffered blips against opponents he was expected to beat, including a defeat by Swiss world number 222 Jerome Kym in Basel last week.

It acted as a reminder of the work he still has to do and the consistency he needs to find.

Ferrero, who will work alongside Shelton's father and current coach Bryan, is regarded as an astute thinker and tactician.

He demands focus and clarity from his charges so they can thrive in the most intense battles. It means he will want the fiery Shelton to play smarter - and perhaps calmer in certain moments - to maximise his weapons.

"Juan Carlos is one of the great minds in tennis," Shelton said.

"His experience of winning at the highest level and developing champions will be a huge asset to our team."

Ferrero has point to prove with 'extraordinary talent'

Ferrero enjoyed a stellar playing career and won the 2003 French Open, but he has become known to a younger generation as the coach who guided Alcaraz to the pinnacle of the sport.

He has largely kept away from the ATP Tour since their sudden split in December last year - but that does not mean he has kept a low profile.

The 45-year-old used his new book to further promote his reputation as a 'supercoach', but can he achieve success with someone other than Alcaraz?

Ferrero always had an eye on coming back in 2027 and held exploratory conversations with a mixture of top-20 stars and younger talents.

Some talks were more serious than others but he did not discuss terms with anyone other than Shelton, who put Ferrero top of the list when considering bringing in another coach.

The plan is for Ferrero to cover 10-12 tournaments next season, including the four Grand Slams.

The pair will begin formally working together during an off-season training block in the United States, although Ferrero will watch Shelton on site at next week's ATP Finals in Turin.

"Ben has extraordinary talent, power and character," Ferrero said.

"I'm looking forward to contributing my experience and working together with everyone to help Ben achieve his ambitions."

How Ferrero gels with Shelton's dad - a former professional player who won two ATP titles - will be key.

Ferrero previously had a six-month spell coaching Zverev, which ended after a third-round Australian Open exit in 2018.

Ferrero was hired by Zverev as an outside voice coming into a father-son coaching dynamic, but the German fired him after claiming Ferrero was "disrespectful" to his team.

Ferrero later said Zverev lacked the professionalism he expected from a top player.

Shelton, known for having a strong work ethic and insatiable will-to-win, is likely to be receptive to Ferrero's demands - as long as they do not neutralise his raw weapons.

But Rick Macci, the veteran American coach who guided the Williams sisters as teenagers, believes Ferrero will find it harder to improve Shelton's technical deficiencies.

"Shelton can win a few Slams if things break his way," Macci said.

"His backhand groundstroke and return can be technically unpredictable - at the top of the mountain the margins are razor thin.

"Ferrero can help a lot in many areas because [Shelton's] backbone is better than his backhand, but getting to number one is a different landscape to mow."

articles.title: Serena Williams conciencia sobre la detección precoz del cáncer de mama
articles.standfirst: Tras realizarse las revisiones pertinentes, la ganadora de 23 títulos de Grand Slam insiste en que "no hay que olvidarse de priorizar la salud mamaria y mantenerse al día con los cribados"
articles.summary: Tras realizarse las revisiones pertinentes, la ganadora de 23 títulos de Grand Slam insiste en que "no hay que olvidarse de priorizar la salud mamaria y mantenerse al día con los cribados"
articles.body: Serena Williams ha alzado la voz. La campeona de 23 títulos de Grand Slam y partícipe en la campaña 'I Touch Myself', que recuerda la importancia de realizarse un control regular mamario, ha colgado un mensaje en sus redes sociales que tiene como objetivo concienciar sobre la salud mamaria de la mujer. Tras realizarse las pruebas pertinentes, Serena ha querido alertar a las mujeres: "Una mañana llena de exámenes de mama. Poniéndome la blusa, quitándomela, poniéndomela, quitándomela. Sé que octubre ya terminó, pero la concienciación sobre el cáncer de mama nunca debería detenerse. Tengo senos muy densos, así que tengo que ser extrameticulosa con mis cribados", escribe la tenista. Aunque octubre sea conocido como el Mes de Sensibilización sobre el Cáncer de Mama, advierte sobre la importancia de la regularidad en los chequeos mamarios. "Señoras, no olviden priorizar su salud mamaria. Háganse el chequeo, conozcan su cuerpo y manténganse al día con sus cribados", cierra Serena en su cuenta de X. La campeona estadounidense lleva inmersa en la lucha contra el cáncer de mama y la defensa de un control regular mamario desde 2018, cuando decidió formar parte de la campaña 'I Touch Myself'.

articles.title: Alcaraz y su lesión: "Hubo momentos en los que dudé de si podría volver a pegar la derecha a mi máximo nivel"
articles.standfirst: El murciano se congratula de haber recuperado su mejor nivel tras la lesión en su muñeca derecha
articles.summary: El murciano se congratula de haber recuperado su mejor nivel tras la lesión en su muñeca derecha
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz ya está en París después de ganar el pasado domingo su cuarto título de la temporada en la pista cubierta de Viena. El murciano ha acudido este lunes al multiusos de La Defense, sede del último Masters 1000, para celebrar los 40 años del torneo. De igual forma, ha atendido a los medios antes de su debut este miércoles con el ganador del partido entre Jiri Lehecka y Alex Michelsen. Alcaraz ha sido sincero en el momento de valorar su brillante regreso a la competición oficial tras haberse perdido algo más de cuatro meses de competición oficial por la lesión en su muñeca derecha. "Estuve mucho tiempo alejado de las pistas y tuve mucho tiempo para pensar y sentir. Hubo momentos en los que estaba seguro de que iba a volver a mi mejor nivel y otros en los que dudé de mí mismo, no voy a mentir, momentos en los que dudé de si podría volver a pegar la derecha a mi máximo nivel, al cien por cien, de si iba a estar físicamente a tope otra vez", reflexiona. "Cuando estás rodeado de grandes profesionales, y crees en tu equipo al cien por cien, es más fácil el regreso. Hemos hecho un buen trabajo y aquí estoy ahora", sentencia. El campeón de siete grandes se deshace en elogios hacia Rafa Jódar, que este lunes ha estrenado su condición de 'top10': "Es increíble lo que está haciendo en su primer año en el circuito. Es fantástico que esté ahí arriba. Estoy muy contento por él. Es un chico muy humilde, una gran persona, que viaja con su padre como entrenador y está consiguiendo grandes cosas. Se merece estar donde está. Me haría ilusión enfrentarme a él algún día, aunque todavía no hemos jugado juntos. Sí hemos coincidido entrenando en los torneos".

articles.summary: El italiano, que se lesionó en los octavos de Viena, es sexto en la Race 2026
articles.body: Flavio Cobolli no ha llegado a tiempo de participar en el Masters 1000 de París. El italiano, que se había visto obligado a abandonar la semana pasada en los octavos del Open 500 de Viena, ha causado este lunes baja de manera oficial en el último TMS del curso. Su ausencia abre aún más la carrera para lograr una de las cuatro plazas restantes para las ATP Finals de Turín (15 al 22). Su lugar en el cuadro lo ocupa el 'lucky loser' Thiago Tirante, que accede directamente a la segunda ronda. Cobolli es ahora mismo sexto de la Race 2026, con 3.690 puntos. Alex de Miñaur, que sería el primer reserva antes de debutar en París, se encuentra a 520 puntos del transalpino. Eso significa que sólo le podría pasar en caso de plantarse en la final del domingo. Flavio no quería arriesgar su lesión muscular con la vista puesta en la cita de maestros y en la posterior fase final de la Copa Davis donde va a ser el número 1 del combinado local, campeón de las tres últimas Ensaladeras de plata.

articles.title: Steffi Graf at 57: Behind 22 Grand Slam titles lies a story of pressure, heartbreak and sacrifice
articles.summary: At 57, Steffi Graf remains one of the most celebrated names in tennis history.
articles.body: At 57, Steffi Graf remains one of the most celebrated names in tennis history. Her achievements still set her apart, from 22 Grand Slam singles titles to an extraordinary 377 weeks at world No. 1. Yet her legacy is not only about records. Graf's career brought intense pressure, public attention and difficult personal moments. After years spent competing at the highest level, she stepped away from professional tennis and built a life that placed family and personal priorities ahead of the spotlight.Steffi Graf's tennis career was shaped by extraordinary pressureGraf became a professional player at just 13. Her rise was rapid, and the expectations grew with every major victory. She eventually reached the top of women's tennis and delivered one of the sport's rarest achievements in 1988, winning all four Grand Slam singles titles and Olympic gold in the same calendar year. That historic Golden Slam remains a defining moment in tennis.But success came with a demanding schedule and constant public attention. Her family also faced difficult scrutiny, including the tax-evasion case involving her father, Peter Graf. In 1993, tennis was shaken by the stabbing of Monica Seles by a spectator obsessed with Graf. The incident was a tragedy that affected the sport and Seles deeply. Graf was not responsible for the attack.Injuries later became another challenge. Still, she found a way to finish her career on a remarkable note. Graf won her 22nd Grand Slam singles title at the 1999 French Open, defeating Martina Hingis in the final. She retired later that year, leaving behind a record that continues to inspire generations of players.Steffi Graf chose family and charity after retirementAway from the tennis court, Graf built a quieter life with fellow tennis champion Andre Agassi. The couple married in 2001 and raised their two children, Jaden and Jaz. Although she no longer competes professionally, Graf has remained connected to charitable work.One of her most significant projects is Children for Tomorrow, an organisation she founded in 1998. It supports children and families affected by war, persecution and forced displacement, offering psychological help and other forms of support.Graf's life after tennis shows that an athlete's identity does not have to remain tied to competition. Her 22 major titles and Golden Slam secured her place in sporting history. Her work beyond the court adds another dimension to that legacy. articles.title: “We have been touched deeply by your..": How Andre Agassi’s emotional tribute brought Steffi Graf to tears during one of their most memorable moment
articles.summary: Steffi Graf had won 22 Grand Slam titles and spent years dominating women's tennis. Yet one of her most emotional moments came away from the court.
articles.body: Steffi Graf had won 22 Grand Slam titles and spent years dominating women's tennis. Yet one of her most emotional moments came away from the court. During her 2004 International Tennis Hall of Fame induction, her husband, Andre Agassi, took the stage to introduce her. What followed was more than a tribute to a tennis champion. His heartfelt words about their relationship left Graf wiping away tears.Agassi did not spend his speech listing her records or celebrating her trophies. Instead, the eight-time Grand Slam champion spoke about the woman behind the achievements. He praised her character, her ability to overcome difficult moments and the life they had built together. Graf later responded with an equally touching message.Andre Agassi's loving words leave Steffi Graf emotional during Hall of Fame ceremonyThe moment took place in 2004 when Graf entered the International Tennis Hall of Fame. Agassi had the honour of introducing his wife, and he made it clear that finding the right words to describe her was not easy."As I attempt to find words worthy to introduce the person that has changed my life, I realize the words have yet to be invented that are large enough, colorful enough, or true enough to express the heart and soul of this woman that I love," Agassi said during his introduction speech.He then spoke about how Graf never allowed her tennis achievements to define her as a person."You have never defined yourself by what you have achieved; rather, you have achieved by how you defined yourself," he said.Agassi also admired how she approached life after retiring from professional tennis in 1999. For him, her decision to embrace motherhood and family life showed the same dedication she had displayed throughout her playing career."And even now, it has taken my breath away to see how you've quietly laid down your racket to pursue love and motherhood, with the same zeal and high standards you have always demanded of yourself," he added.However, his tribute did not stop there. Agassi also remembered Graf's ability to overcome adversity, play through injuries and return to winning ways."The history books will record for posterity, your ability to embrace and rise above adversity, to play through injury, and to win again, and again, and again," he said.Graf had been wiping away tears throughout the ceremony. Hearing her husband speak about her beyond her achievements made the occasion even more personal. Steffi Graf's beautiful response makes Andre Agassi's tribute unforgettableWhen Graf stepped forward to accept the honour, she had a special message for Agassi. Rather than simply thanking him for the introduction, she spoke about what meeting him had meant to her."Not that this occasion isn't emotional enough, to hear how much you are loved is amazing," Graf said during her acceptance speech.She then looked towards her husband and delivered one of the most touching lines of the ceremony."The best part of the tour is I ran into you. I'll be forever grateful for that," she added.Agassi saved his biggest declaration for the end of his introduction. He spoke about the impact Graf had made on him and their family."We have been touched deeply by your life, you have made us better, and we will never be the same," he said.He then introduced her as "the greatest person I've ever known."The couple had married in October 2001 and welcomed their son, Jaden, that same year. Their daughter, Jaz, was born in 2003. Their relationship had also grown beyond their shared tennis careers, giving Agassi another reason to admire the woman he had introduced that day.Seven years after Graf's induction, Agassi also entered the International Tennis Hall of Fame in 2011. Together, they have won 30 Grand Slam singles titles. Yet their 2004 ceremony offered something no trophy could capture: a public reminder of how deeply two tennis champions valued each other.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
